teaser.text: Nucor is a steel company, but its business begins before a coil leaves a mill and ends after steel has become part of a building, machine or data center. To understand how a dollar moves through it, follow the metal from scrap and iron to sale, customer, factory and shareholder.

stock.opening: Nucor's weighted forecast points to $278.02 in October 2027 and $357.36 in October 2029. It hinges on steel earnings recovery, West Virginia execution and cash generation that supports buybacks.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Nucor's business works, who its rivals are, how management is allocating capital and which risks could change the outcome.

blocks.heading: Where could Nucor's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to moderate gains in the central path, with substantial downside if the steel recovery fails. The probability-weighted price is $278.02 in October 2027, $307.99 in October 2028 and $357.36 in October 2029. Including dividends, those returns are 9%, 22% and 42% from today’s $256.29.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Nucor?

paragraphs.text: The first target implies a 9% return including dividends; the last implies 42%. Bear probability is 29%. Base probability is 52%. Bull probability is 19%. Imports, construction demand, customer qualification—buyer approval that the mill's steel meets requirements—and profitable new capacity decide the outcome. Nucor's next results release is scheduled for October 26, 2026; operating cash flow, remaining capital spending and performance against Q3 guidance are the near-term tests. West Virginia commercial shipments are expected in early 2027, with utilization and product offerings building through 2027 and 2028. Remember: buybacks reduced average diluted shares by 3.1% in 2025, but share-count reduction cannot replace improving per-ton economics.

The base path uses $7,300M in the first forecast year and $8,200M in the second. It reaches $8,500M in the final year. The bear path falls to $4,200M in the middle year before recovering to $5,000M. The bull path reaches $8,800M first and $11,000M last. The recent operating recovery supports the base case: first-half operating income implies an annualized EBITDA pace near $6,954M, although a $130M procurement refund will not recur. The West Virginia mill is expected to begin commercial shipments in early 2027 and build utilization through 2028.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Nucor really make?

paragraphs.text: Cash from operations reflects customer receipts, operating payments and changes in receivables, inventory and payables. Free cash flow subtracts capital spending. Stock compensation is not a current-period cash payment, but subtracting it gives a stricter measure because shareholders ultimately bear dilution.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Nucor today?

paragraphs.text: The P/E, or price-to-earnings ratio, compares the share price with the earnings produced for each share. The forward P/E is lower than the trailing P/E, which means the valuation assumes earnings will recover. Price-to-book compares the share price with the accounting value of shareholders’ equity. Enterprise value measures the operating business after adding debt and subtracting cash.

dividend.opening: Nucor’s current quarterly rate is $0.56, implying an annual pace of $2.24. Recent payouts have run ahead of the cash Nucor’s operations generated, so free cash flow has not fully covered them.
dividend.closing: The full Nucor memo also explains Nucor’s business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Nucor pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The dividend is the steadiest driver. The current quarterly rate is $0.56, implying an annual pace of $2.24. Base dividends rise to $2.28 in the second year and $2.32 in the final year. The bear case holds at $2.24, while the bull case reaches $2.40. The base path follows the record of annual increases, but the bear case allows a pause because 2025 free cash flow was negative $188M during heavy investment.

blocks.heading: Does Nucor’s dividend come from its cash?

paragraphs.text: In the latest two years, Nucor paid shareholders more than free cash flow. That is possible because free cash flow is not a legal spending limit: the company can draw down cash, borrow, sell assets or use other financing. The choice still matters because shareholder returns then compete with the West Virginia mill, acquisitions, debt repayment and liquidity.

earnings.meta_description: Nucor’s next results are scheduled for October 26, 2026; see guidance, recent results and what to watch.
earnings.opening: Nucor’s next results are scheduled for October 26, 2026. Watch operating cash flow and progress against management’s earnings range.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers what Nucor does, who its rivals are, how its management works, and what risks it faces.

paragraphs.text: For the third quarter ending October 2026, management guided to $5.55–$5.65 per diluted share. It also expects full-year shipment growth, without giving a numerical range in the guide.

Nucor’s policy is to return at least 40% of annual net earnings through dividends and share repurchases. Because the amount depends on earnings, this is a policy commitment rather than a fixed cash bill.

blocks.heading: Has Nucor kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Buybacks exceeded stock pay in each year shown, and diluted shares fell in the two most recent years shown. That supports shareholder alignment, although buybacks still create value only when Nucor buys at sensible prices.

blocks.heading: What do Nucor’s last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue, gross margin and diluted EPS all rose from Q2 2025. The improvement came from both price and volume: average price per ton rose 10%, while external tons rose 12%. Steel-mill shipments reached a record level, while steel-products growth was led by tubular products and rebar fabrication rather than every product line.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Nucor’s next results?

paragraphs.text: Nucor’s next results release is scheduled for October 26, 2026. Investors should look for operating cash flow, remaining capital spending and progress against the third-quarter earnings range. The longer test is whether commissioning becomes saleable steel and whether commercial production begins as planned in 2027.
